concept_prompts:
Use case: identity-preserve / weapon replacement.
Edit this EXACT yellow-brown fox-eared teenage girl into the game's PROTAGONIST with a GREAT SWORD as her starting weapon. The user's clarification is: 这是主角角色，我希望他初始用大剑. Preserve her youthful cheerful face, light natural teenage build, honey-golden hair with short side ponytail, chocolate-tipped fox ears, amber eyes, one fluffy golden-brown tail with a cream tip, mustard cape, ivory high-neck long-sleeved tunic fully covering the torso, simple chestnut vest, practical shorts over completely opaque brown tights, fingerless gloves and sturdy boots. Retain the SAME modest outfit, warm palette and coarse pixel style. Do not age her up or change her identity.
REPLACE the bow, bowstring, arrows and quiver completely. Her only weapon is ONE clearly oversized TWO-HANDED GREAT SWORD, about 70–80% of her standing height, with a broad straight steel blade, simple angular tip, readable pale silver edge and blue-gray steel shadow, a restrained brass crossguard and a long chestnut leather grip big enough for two hands. Plain sturdy beginner weapon, no glowing magic, no ornate jewels. She holds the hilt in a relaxed ready stance beside her body, blade angled downward beside one boot, fully visible and distinctly separated from her large fox tail. Slightly open balanced stance suitable for a protagonist's idle pose, friendly determined smile. Both arms and hands are anatomically clear, no extra weapons.
CRITICAL pixel style: coarse hand-authored retro fantasy game sprite, approximately 96 x 144 logical pixels for the entire figure, enlarged with nearest-neighbor presentation; large square pixels, visible stair-step dark plum-indigo 1-pixel outline, chunky connected color clusters, simplified hair and folds, only 2–3 flat shades per material, limited soft palette. Honey yellow, caramel, chestnut and cream dominate the character, steel grays only on the sword. No tiny trim, no thin smooth linework, no gradients, no blur, no anti-aliasing, no painterly textures or 3D shading.
Composition: ONE full-body character, all ears, sword blade and tail completely inside the portrait frame with comfortable margin. Truly transparent alpha background. Remove background aura and haze. No scenery, shadow, text, panels, labels or watermark.

Use case: precise-object-edit.
Correct ONLY the geometry of the sword's handle and the two hands holding it. The user noticed that the grip is crooked. This is a construction error: the existing handle bends left above the guard, while the blade's centerline continues up toward the right. Fix it mechanically.
Preserve the EXACT character, youthful face, hair, ears, tail, modest fully covering outfit, colors, full-body composition, and low-resolution chunky pixel-art rendering. Preserve the broad steel blade's existing size and downward-left direction.
The sword is ONE completely STRAIGHT rigid object. Its pommel center, leather grip center, crossguard midpoint, center ridge of the blade, and blade tip MUST lie on ONE uninterrupted straight diagonal axis. Starting at the blade tip in the lower-left, extend the blade centerline straight up and RIGHT through the crossguard and through the grip to the pommel. The grip must therefore extend toward the upper-RIGHT from the crossguard, NOT toward the upper-left. Draw a simple straight cylindrical brown two-hand grip with parallel sides and one brass pommel at the end. No bend, no crooked joint, no offset at the guard. The straight crossguard is perpendicular to this same sword axis.
Reposition her gloved hands and slightly adjust her forearms only as needed so BOTH hands grip this corrected STRAIGHT handle naturally, one closer to the crossguard, one closer to the pommel. Keep all fingers anatomically sensible and the hilt visible between hands. Do not make the blade follow a bent handle; keep the blade direction and correct the handle to the blade. Use a unified straight centerline as the construction guide, but do not show any guide line in the final image.
Keep every other detail unchanged. Hard square pixels, dark plum outlines, no added fine detail or antialiasing. Genuinely transparent alpha background, no visible glow, haze, scenery, text or watermark.

Use case: precise-object-edit.
Fix the sword definitively by changing the ENTIRE sword to a perfectly UPRIGHT VERTICAL orientation at the LEFT side of the image. The previous diagonal grip still did not align correctly. Keep the girl, face, hair, fox ears, tail, outfit, low-resolution pixel style and palette unchanged; adjust only the sword and her hands/forearms to hold it.
Draw one plain mechanically correct two-handed greatsword straight vertical, blade tip pointing directly DOWN and nearly touching the ground beside her left boot. The pommel is directly ABOVE the grip, directly ABOVE the midpoint of a HORIZONTAL crossguard, directly ABOVE the central ridge and the tip of the steel blade. ALL these centers have the SAME horizontal coordinate. The hilt must be one uninterrupted straight vertical brown bar. Symmetrical brass pommel cap at the top. Long straight parallel-sided chestnut leather grip, no bend or offset. One simple symmetrical horizontal brass crossguard. Broad straight symmetrical steel blade extends vertically down from the EXACT center of that guard, with parallel edges and a simple symmetrical tapered point at its bottom. The blade and handle form a single perfectly straight vertical axis. No diagonal sword or perspective foreshortening.
Her two gloved hands hold that SAME vertical handle stacked one above the other, in front of her left side at around waist/hip height. Show the straight brown handle emerging above the upper hand with its pommel, between the hands, and below the lower hand before the crossguard. The blade stays fully outside her legs, clearly separated from her body silhouette. Both arms reach naturally to the handle. Preserve the same broad sword proportions, a blade almost as long as her legs and torso together. Full sword, pommel and point inside frame.
Same youthful cheerful fox-eared girl with fully covering ivory tunic, mustard cape, brown vest and shorts over opaque tights, sturdy boots. Hard large square pixels, flat color blocks, stepped dark outline, no new fine detail. Genuinely transparent alpha background, no text or watermark. Do not add any bow, arrows, second sword, sheath or magical effects.

sprite_prompts.common: Production low-resolution game sprite sheet of the EXACT SAME youthful fox-eared teenage protagonist in the reference. Keep her light youthful build and round cheerful face, honey-golden side ponytail, two chocolate-tipped fox ears, amber eyes, ONE fluffy golden-brown tail with cream tip, mustard short cape, fully covering ivory high-neck long-sleeved tunic, simple chestnut vest, brown shorts over fully opaque brown tights, fingerless gloves and sturdy brown boots. The starter weapon is ONE broad straight two-handed steel greatsword with plain brass guard and long straight brown leather grip. No bow, arrows or quiver. CRITICAL weapon anatomy: pommel, grip, guard midpoint, blade central ridge and blade tip ALWAYS on one straight axis, in every frame. Guard perpendicular to blade. No crooked hilt or separate handle angles. BOTH hands grip the same straight hilt naturally. Keep sword proportions the same as reference, broad and about 75% of standing character height. Coarse hand-pixeled retro fantasy style, character body about 100-112 logical pixels high, large square pixels, stepped dark plum 1-pixel outline, flat 2-3 shade clusters per material, limited warm yellow-brown-cream palette with plain steel grays on sword. No gradients, fine ornaments, soft edges, smooth linework, painterly textures or detailed noise. Same body size and camera throughout. Right-facing three-quarter side view with readable face, tail trailing left; same ONE sword in every pose. Each full figure plus ALL of its sword and tail stays inside its own region, with LARGE transparent gutters. Do not let adjacent poses touch or overlap. Do not put the sword tip below the boot baseline in standing poses. For each pose leave enough room above the head for a raised greatsword. True alpha transparency, no background, glow, aura, shadow, grid lines, numbers, labels, text, watermark, particles or slash trails.

specs.prompt: Exactly 12 full-body sprites arranged 4 columns x 3 rows, left-to-right reading order. ROW 1: 4 subtle idle breathing poses forming a loop, feet planted, both hands resting on upright greatsword hilt, broad blade points straight down beside body with tip at boot baseline, tail sways slightly. ROW 2: 4 hurt recoil poses, wince and draw sword close while knees bend, then recover; no blood. ROW 3: 4 defeat poses, knees buckle, kneel, slump sideways, lie resting with sword resting beside her; no injury detail. All four defeat poses distinctly lower and collapse. Keep clothing modest and character design consistent.

Exactly 8 full-body sprites arranged 4 columns x 2 rows, read as one continuous RIGHTWARD run cycle: right leg leading contact, compression, passing, flight; left leg leading contact, compression, passing, flight. Clearly alternate which leg leads. Carry the ONE straight greatsword low and diagonally behind or close to the body with BOTH hands on its hilt, blade pointing safely behind; keep its shape rigid, no bending. Cape hair and tail stream left. Planted feet share a baseline; flight rises only a couple logical pixels. No repeated standing poses.

Exactly 8 full-body sprites arranged 4 columns x 2 rows, read left-to-right as one right-facing heavy GREAT SWORD attack sequence: 1 grounded two-hand ready guard, 2 draw back, 3 raise the entire straight sword above shoulder, 4 strongest overhead wind-up, 5 step forward with a powerful downward diagonal slash, 6 low follow-through sword fully extended forward, 7 begin recovering, 8 return to ready guard. Show clear changes in arm and sword angle and body weight; tail balances behind to the left. Both hands stay on ONE straight hilt; blade and hilt remain rigidly collinear in all 8 poses. No detached weapon, slash effects, glow, projectiles or extra swords. Large transparent room above and beside every pose prevents clipping.

Exactly 12 full-body sprites arranged 4 columns x 3 rows. Left-to-right reading order. ROW 1: anticipation crouch, upward takeoff, rising legs bent, rising with cape/tail trailing downward. ROW 2: apex tucked legs, apex relaxing legs, descent knees bent, descent feet reaching downward. ROW 3: feet touch down, deep landing crouch, standing recovery, final upright idle guard. Hold ONE straight greatsword close diagonally with BOTH hands throughout; do not stretch sword beyond cell. Keep torso/head at a stable cell height in airborne poses; physical game movement supplies jump displacement. Neutral final pose matches reference, sword tip at boot baseline. Consistent scale and sword design across all poses.
